title: What went through his mind when soloing
summary: Bunn does not know how he thought when soloing; he says the secret is the ear, not reading notes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Uh-huh. When you were soloing, how -- what were you thinking, or how were you thinking?
How was I thinking? Now,that's the $64.00 question.
Because I don't know how the hell I was thinking either.
I mean, some people think colors, you know, or patterns.
Sometimes when I solo I think about as if I was talking.
Trying to say something, you know?
But say it with the sound instead of with the word.
I've talked to different people about this, and everybody has a different idea, you know?
Well, some people say they think in terms of a certain scale, you know, and like walking around, like they're in a new room and they walk around inside and check pick out the furniture.
Some people talk about like as if they were singing, you know like they're singing some words, but they put it into the notes instead of --
And I just wondered like what kinds of things go through your mind when you solo?
Now, that's what I'm thinking now, what kind of stuff was going through my mind, but to tell you the
truth, my mind was in an uproar.
The way it felt to me, my mind was in an uproar, but I still brought them things out.
Evidently I ended on them things I was thinking last, evidently.
You mean kind of like a soup or a gumbo, and you pick things out of it?
Yeah. And I ate the last bite, you know, and that was it.
Solid. Well, that's -- people are different, you know.

I didn't know what the hell I was playing, to tell you the truth. I didn't know what I was playing. They'd tell me what number to play, and if I knew it I'd just play it. And whatever I wanted to put in, anything come into my mind as I'm playing, I put it in, to make it sound right.
That's right, that is the secret. Because when the guys got them notes reading in front of them, it's in their minds they've still got to play them notes that they've got.
If it's wrong, they hit the wrong note on their instrument. Can you figure that out? That's what they did.
But me, I didn't care if it was wrong or not, as long as it felt right to me.
As long as I heard it. And the majority would show you that's what that ear's for.
